status: PROPOSAL - research data only. This file is NOT authoritative simulation state and NOT renderer presentation data. It does not finalise a runtime schema. Canonical settlement/location identities (RFC 4122 UUIDv5, ADR-0009) are minted only by the atlas pipeline at integration time; the proposedId values here are research handles, not canonical IDs.
subject: R-16 historical settlement roster, fourth batch (batch 4)
envelopeRegions: 1 - Italy, Sicily & the islands (incl. Cisalpine Gaul) - northern-Italy interior gap-fill (mid ~100); 6 - Balkans & Thrace (incl. Illyria, Dacia/Getae) (mid ~52)
batchScope: A ten-record completion of envelope region 1 focused on Cisalpine Gaul and the northern Italian interior, and 52 records for envelope region 6 (Illyria, Dalmatia/Liburnia, Pannonia, Macedonia, Thrace, the western Black Sea coast and the Dacia/Getae fringe)
coordinateConvention: WGS84 decimal degrees, approximate representative points for the ancient site (not the modern town unless noted). Precision does not imply archaeological accuracy and is not a surveyed building location.
idScheme: proposedId = r16-ita-<slug> for envelope region 1 additions (northern Italy/Cisalpine Gaul) or r16-bal-<slug> for envelope region 6 (Balkans & Thrace); the slug (key) is region-scoped to avoid homonyms. Stable, human-readable, non-canonical.
methodNote: Records are compiled from independent evidence (primary literary/administrative sources, archaeology and the Pleiades gazetteer for coordinates). Game/mod faction names are discovery leads only and never authorities. Every coordinate is a representative point with an explicit location confidence; where only a broad location is known the coordinate is coarse or null. Political authority is recorded only where supported; otherwise it is left unclaimed.
sourceAuditNote: Pleiades gazetteer identifiers are recorded only as 'to be confirmed', never asserted: automated access to pleiades.stoa.org was blocked by the site's anti-scraping protection during this pass, so no Pleiades id has been verified. Coordinates are approximate representative points, not surveyed locations. All literary sources (Herodotus, Thucydides, Xenophon, Polybius, Livy, Diodorus, Strabo, Appian, Plutarch, Pliny, Ptolemy) are later than 278 BCE and are dated in each record; they are evidence for continuity, not contemporary snapshots. Confirming Pleiades ids and site coordinates manually remains an integration prerequisite.
politicalContext278Bce: 278 BCE is a year of acute flux in the northern and eastern Balkans. The great Gallic (Galatian) invasion is under way: after ravaging Thrace and Macedon and attacking Delphi (279), Galatian warbands cross the Hellespont into Anatolia in 278/277. Macedon is in dynastic chaos: Ptolemy Keraunos was killed by the Gauls (279) and Antigonus Gonatas is not yet recognised king (he defeats the Gauls at Lysimachia in 277, king by c. 276). Thrace is fragmented among Thracian dynasts (the Odrysian sphere around Seuthopolis) with incoming Celtic settlement (Tylis; the Scordisci in the central Balkans). Illyria is a patchwork of tribal powers (Labeatae, Ardiaei, Delmatae, Liburni, Histri, Bylliones, Dassaretae); the Ardiaean kingdom has not yet reached its 250s-230s peak, and the Adriatic Greek colonies (Epidamnos, Apollonia, Issa, Pharos) remain autonomous poleis. Epirus under Pyrrhus is preoccupied in Italy and Sicily until 275. In the west, Rome has defeated the Senones and Boii (283) but has not yet subdued Cisalpine Gaul: the Insubres (Mediolanum) and the Venetic and Cenomanian allies occupy the Po plain, and Latin colonies such as Ariminum (268) and Aquileia (181) lie in the future. Later Roman provinces (Macedonia 148, Dalmatia, Moesia, Pannonia, Dacia) and later refoundations must NOT be retrojected.
duplicateGuard: None of these records reproduce the 23 active atlas sites, the 12 deferred atlas candidates, the excluded site (Cosa), the 55 batch-1 central-Mediterranean records, or the 56 batch-2 Greece/Aegean/Anatolia/Black-Sea records. The id prefixes r16-ita- and r16-bal- are disjoint from r16-gre- and r16-ana-. Byzantium (r16-ana-byzantium) is deliberately left to batch 2; southern Epirus is left to envelope region 7.

records.architectureContext: An open Gallic oppidum in the central Po plain; the later Roman circuit walls and street grid are subsequent phases.
